evidence_packet.evidence_text: Almost £1bn government cash to North West for 7,500 new homes - BBC News Image source, EPA/Shutterstock By Hannah Richardson Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago The government is to give nearly £1bn to the North West to deliver about 7,500 new homes as part of plans to "build the country out of a housing crisis". A share of up to £10bn has been announced for councils and housing associations nationally in the first wave of government funding to boost "genuinely affordable homes". Greater Manchester has been given the largest share of the six mayoral areas to benefit from this round, with Liverpool City Region set to deliver 3,100 homes supported by £380m. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged the largest post-war council housebuilding programme to tackle severe shortages and homelessness, saying "no child should be raised in a hostel room". Nationally, almost 180,000 children are growing up without a permanent home, according to the government. The Prime Minister said the cash will go to regional mayors, councils, housing associations and other providers, and will be spent on building "genuinely affordable homes". Around 60% of the more than 70,000 properties are expected to be social rent. They will be in the first wave of Labour's £39bn 10-year Social and Affordable Homes Programme , external . The government said it aimed to help families "trapped in temporary accommodation or stuck on housing waiting lists' into safe, secure homes". Image caption, Liverpool City Region is set to deliver 3,100 homes Burnham said: "No child should be raised in a hostel room and no family should wait ten years for a front door of their own. title: Debt-ridden Warrington Borough Council announces £51.2m more cuts

evidence_packet.title: Debt-ridden Warrington Borough Council announces £51.2m more cuts
evidence_packet.lead: The additional savings plan brings the total cuts to about £90m
evidence_packet.summary: The additional savings plan brings the total cuts to about £90m
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cash-strapped Warrington Borough Council is planning more than £50m of extra cuts It is set to publish a report detailing a further £51.2m of savings which, alongside £39m of cuts previously identified by the authority in March, brings the total to about £90m This included ending funding for walking day, selling off assets, cutting street lighting and stopping free parking in the town centre The Labour administration said the cuts were aimed at "ensuring the council's future sustainability", but the Liberal Democrats said there was "little confidence" in the administration The new savings proposals will be discussed at the council's scrutiny committee on 7 September, before being considered for approval by cabinet and endorsement by full council The council's cabinet member for finance, councillor Denis Matthews, said the council faced a £179m funding gap up to 2030

title: Oldham community garden's food supply hit by dry summer

evidence_packet.title: Oldham community garden's food supply hit by dry summer
evidence_packet.lead: A community garden in Oldham has lost three quarters of plants, fruit and vegetables due to hot weather
evidence_packet.summary: A community garden in Oldham has lost three quarters of plants, fruit and vegetables due to hot weather
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A community garden has been forced to throw away food which was destined for the local community as a result of recent dry weather Volunteers from Northern Lily Community Hub in Oldham said up to three quarters of its plants, fruit and vegetables simply did not survive the hot summer "Normally we grow over a tonne of food which equates to 12,700 meals worth and we give that away to our community," Victoria Holden from the garden said "Unfortunately, I'm not sure we'll get to a tonne this year and that's real fresh food that normally supports our community which is now not going to be available." "We lost a lot of plants. We had to just reduce everything down in the polytunnel to what could cope with that sometimes 55 degree heat," she said Holden said tropical plants like the chillies, gourds, aubergines and tomatoes had survived but the produce was "about a quarter full to where it would normally be at this stage in the year"

title: Mum 'super proud' of Macclesfield teen who passed GCSEs using eyes

evidence_packet.title: Mum 'super proud' of Macclesfield teen who passed GCSEs using eyes
evidence_packet.lead: Patrick McCabe, 16, used eye-tracking technology to take his GCSEs over a five-month period
evidence_packet.summary: Patrick McCabe, 16, used eye-tracking technology to take his GCSEs over a five-month period
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mum of a teenager with cerebral palsy who passed his GCSEs by using eye-tracking technology has said she is "super proud" of his achievement Patrick McCabe, 16, from Cheshire, took seven GCSE exams between February and June and got the grades he needed to go on to sixth form and study A-levels His mum Jo praised his "patience and willpower", adding the exams were difficult enough to do, but "having to do them with his eyes is an even bigger challenge" Patrick said when he opened his results he "thought they mixed me up with someone else", but after double checking his name at the top he "felt relieved that all the work I did prior to my exams paid off" He said his most difficult subject was maths, "because I had to do the workings out in my head" "I found it frustrating that I couldn't just write on to the paper," he told BBC Breakfast

title: Mum says painful condition 'overlooked' during pregnancy

evidence_packet.title: Mum says painful condition 'overlooked' during pregnancy
evidence_packet.lead: Grace, 28, has spoken out about her traumatic pregnancy in the hope others do not suffer the same ordeal
evidence_packet.summary: Grace, 28, has spoken out about her traumatic pregnancy in the hope others do not suffer the same ordeal
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mum who suffered from pre-eclampsia during pregnancy said she felt her symptoms were "overlooked" due to her underlying sickle cell disease Grace, 28, from Manchester, was in her second trimester when she started noticing how "physically taxing" her pregnancy had become including "extreme pain" It was only when she was admitted to St Mary's Hospital in Manchester with a sickle cell disease (SCD) unit that she was diagnosed with pre-eclampsia, a pregnancy-related condition that can cause high blood pressure, and went on to have an emergency Caesarean She has called for urgent research and more awareness of SCD so people do not suffer the same trauma ordeal she did She said: "It's not often you get pre-eclampsia present itself and not be flagged up "It was just something that was so overlooked that any symptom that was raised or any issue that was raised, they just put it down to sickle cell."

evidence_packet.title: Mum to travel to US over Lucy Harrison shooting investigation

evidence_packet.summary: Jane Coates says she hopes to meet the district attorney and call for the investigation to be reopened
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mother of a British woman who was unlawfully killed after being shot by her father in Texas is preparing to travel to the US to try to persuade prosecutors to reopen the investigation into her death Lucy Harrison, 23, from Warrington, was shot in the chest on 10 January 2025 in Prosper, near Dallas Police in the town investigated her death as possible manslaughter but no criminal case was brought against her father Kris Harrison after a grand jury in Collin County declined to indict him Lucy Harrison's mother Jane Coates said she hopes to meet the district attorney and call for a fresh investigation. The Collin County District Attorney's Office has been approached for comment Harrison, a 23-year-old fashion buyer, was shot by her father at his home in Texas the day before she was due to fly home to the UK A grand jury in Collin County later decided there was insufficient evidence to bring criminal charges after Kris Harrison said the Glock handgun discharged accidentally while he was showing it to his daughter

They have been using their share of a £15m funding pot from Historic England, aimed at rescuing historic buildings from dereliction or demolition. Among the sites to get money were Salford Lads and Girls Club in Greater Manchester, and Morecambe's Winter Gardens. Historic England said the work to bring new life to heritage "can help build a better future for people and places". Morecambe Winter Gardens Winter Gardens was given £767,222 to fix the structure and staircases. The theatre's preservation trust said that the 19th-century building had been "stabilised" by the repairs. "That sounds quite extreme, but it was a major piece of structural engineering we needed to do," said Prof Vanessa Toulmin, chair of Morecambe Winter Gardens. Image source, Morecambe Winter Gardens Image caption, Morecambe Winter Gardens had about 50 volunteers who helped with the project The theatre was opened in 1897, before closing its doors in 1977 and remaining shut for almost four decades. Toulmin said the completed work meant the theatre could continue plans to expand its capacity to more than 1,200 people. "It just gives people in Morecambe a lot of pride, but it also ensures the building is still a place for them." evidence_packet.summary: Hayley Metcalfe, 37, suffered the loss of two babies at 17 and 19 weeks into the pregnancies
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mum wants people to know 'there is hope after pregnancy loss' - BBC News Image source, Family handout Image caption, Hayley and Mike Metcalfe welcomed baby Hope earlier this year By Georgie Docker North West Published 24 August 2026 A woman who welcomed a daughter after two pregnancy losses has said she wants others who face similar heartache to know "there is still hope". Hayley Metcalfe, 37, from Runcorn in Cheshire, said she and her husband Mike were "over the moon" to find out she was pregnant with her second son in 2023. But what followed was three years of heartbreak when Hayley suffered a placental abruption at 19 weeks pregnant and was told her baby boy, who they had named Oscar, had died. The following year, the couple lost a second baby, who they had named Leo, at 17 weeks pregnant. "The road after baby loss is never easy and trusting again can feel impossible," said Hayley. "But I want people to know there can still be hope." Image source, Handout Image caption, Hayley and Mike Metcalfe had their youngest child Hope via C-section in February Hayley said the couple had always wanted to start a family and, in 2019, the pair welcomed their eldest son George. She recalled how she had a normal pregnancy with George so when she fell pregnant again in 2023, her and husband Mike were excited to grow their family. But at 19 weeks and four days into her pregnancy, Hayley said she felt as though "something wasn't right". An ultrasound later confirmed that Oscar had died. "It sounds awful, but when you know your baby is no longer alive, you just want it all to be over," she said. "We already had so many baby things at home. "I just couldn't bear to look at them. title: Why police are flying drones over Manchester's railway tracks

evidence_packet.title: Why police are flying drones over Manchester's railway tracks
evidence_packet.lead: The remotely operated aircraft can patrol lines for trespassers, reducing potential train delays
evidence_packet.summary: The remotely operated aircraft can patrol lines for trespassers, reducing potential train delays
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police drones are being launched remotely over railway lines in Manchester as part of a scheme aimed at finding trespassers and reducing delays The aircraft are kept in weatherproof boxes at sites beside the railway and can be launched remotely by pilots based in London when an incident is reported Since the British Transport Police (BTP) launched its first site in Leeds in April 2025, four sites have been introduced across south London, as well as sites in Leicester and Manchester The BPT said Manchester was chosen because it is a known hotspot for trespass and disruption A pilot does not need to be on or near the site before the drone can take off, and the drone can also be used proactively - to patrol areas where intelligence suggests trespassing may be taking place BTP hopes to establish further sites in the North West as it expands the programme, although no additional locations have been announced so far

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cash-strapped Warrington Borough Council is planning more than £50m of extra cuts It is set to publish a report detailing a further £51.2m of savings which, alongside £39m of cuts previously identified by the authority in March, brings the total to about £90m This included ending funding for walking day, selling off assets, cutting street lighting and stopping free parking in the town centre The Labour administration said the cuts were aimed at "ensuring the council's future sustainability", but the Liberal Democrats said there was "little confidence" in the administration The new savings proposals will be discussed at the council's scrutiny committee on 7 September, before being considered for approval by cabinet and endorsement by full council The council's cabinet member for finance, councillor Denis Matthews, said the council faced a £179m funding gap up to 2030

evidence_packet.summary: A community garden has been forced to throw away food which was destined for the local community as a result of recent dry weather Volunteers from Northern Lily Community Hub in Oldham said up to three quarters of its plants, fruit and vegetables simply did not survive the hot su
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A community garden has been forced to throw away food which was destined for the local community as a result of recent dry weather Volunteers from Northern Lily Community Hub in Oldham said up to three quarters of its plants, fruit and vegetables simply did not survive the hot summer "Normally we grow over a tonne of food which equates to 12,700 meals worth and we give that away to our community," Victoria Holden from the garden said "Unfortunately, I'm not sure we'll get to a tonne this year and that's real fresh food that normally supports our community which is now not going to be available." "We lost a lot of plants. We had to just reduce everything down in the polytunnel to what could cope with that sometimes 55 degree heat," she said Holden said tropical plants like the chillies, gourds, aubergines and tomatoes had survived but the produce was "about a quarter full to where it would normally be at this stage in the year"

title: Mum 'super proud' of Macclesfield teen who passed GCSEs using eyes

evidence_packet.title: Mum 'super proud' of Macclesfield teen who passed GCSEs using eyes
evidence_packet.lead: The mum of a teenager with cerebral palsy who passed his GCSEs by using eye-tracking technology has said she is "super proud" of his achievement Patrick McCabe, 16, from Cheshire, took seven GCSE exams between February and June and got the grades he needed to go on to sixth form
evidence_packet.summary: The mum of a teenager with cerebral palsy who passed his GCSEs by using eye-tracking technology has said she is "super proud" of his achievement Patrick McCabe, 16, from Cheshire, took seven GCSE exams between February and June and got the grades he needed to go on to sixth form
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mum of a teenager with cerebral palsy who passed his GCSEs by using eye-tracking technology has said she is "super proud" of his achievement Patrick McCabe, 16, from Cheshire, took seven GCSE exams between February and June and got the grades he needed to go on to sixth form and study A-levels His mum Jo praised his "patience and willpower", adding the exams were difficult enough to do, but "having to do them with his eyes is an even bigger challenge" Patrick said when he opened his results he "thought they mixed me up with someone else", but after double checking his name at the top he "felt relieved that all the work I did prior to my exams paid off" He said his most difficult subject was maths, "because I had to do the workings out in my head" "I found it frustrating that I couldn't just write on to the paper," he told BBC Breakfast

title: Mum says painful condition 'overlooked' during pregnancy

evidence_packet.title: Mum says painful condition 'overlooked' during pregnancy
evidence_packet.lead: A mum who suffered from pre-eclampsia during pregnancy said she felt her symptoms were "overlooked" due to her underlying sickle cell disease Grace, 28, from Manchester, was in her second trimester when she started noticing how "physically taxing" her pregnancy had become includi
evidence_packet.summary: A mum who suffered from pre-eclampsia during pregnancy said she felt her symptoms were "overlooked" due to her underlying sickle cell disease Grace, 28, from Manchester, was in her second trimester when she started noticing how "physically taxing" her pregnancy had become includi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A mum who suffered from pre-eclampsia during pregnancy said she felt her symptoms were "overlooked" due to her underlying sickle cell disease Grace, 28, from Manchester, was in her second trimester when she started noticing how "physically taxing" her pregnancy had become including "extreme pain" It was only when she was admitted to St Mary's Hospital in Manchester with a sickle cell disease (SCD) unit that she was diagnosed with pre-eclampsia, a pregnancy-related condition that can cause high blood pressure, and went on to have an emergency Caesarean She has called for urgent research and more awareness of SCD so people do not suffer the same trauma ordeal she did She said: "It's not often you get pre-eclampsia present itself and not be flagged up "It was just something that was so overlooked that any symptom that was raised or any issue that was raised, they just put it down to sickle cell."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The mother of a British woman who was unlawfully killed after being shot by her father in Texas is preparing to travel to the US to try to persuade prosecutors to reopen the investigation into her death Lucy Harrison, 23, from Warrington, was shot in the chest on 10 January 2025 in Prosper, near Dallas Police in the town investigated her death as possible manslaughter but no criminal case was brought against her father Kris Harrison after a grand jury in Collin County declined to indict him Lucy Harrison's mother Jane Coates said she hopes to meet the district attorney and call for a fresh investigation. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Police drones are being launched remotely over railway lines in Manchester as part of a scheme aimed at finding trespassers and reducing delays The aircraft are kept in weatherproof boxes at sites beside the railway and can be launched remotely by pilots based in London when an incident is reported Since the British Transport Police (BTP) launched its first site in Leeds in April 2025, four sites have been introduced across south London, as well as sites in Leicester and Manchester The BPT said Manchester was chosen because it is a known hotspot for trespass and disruption A pilot does not need to be on or near the site before the drone can take off, and the drone can also be used proactively - to patrol areas where intelligence suggests trespassing may be taking place BTP hopes to establish further sites in the North West as it expands the programme, although no additional locations have been announced so far

title: Rectal cancer trial offers non-surgical treatment hope

evidence_packet.title: Rectal cancer trial offers non-surgical treatment hope
evidence_packet.lead: A major trial has found that patients with rectal cancer may be able to avoid major surgery and the need for a colostomy bag Led by the Universities of Leeds and Birmingham, the international trial treated patients with early-stage rectal cancer, with combinations of chemotherapy
evidence_packet.summary: A major trial has found that patients with rectal cancer may be able to avoid major surgery and the need for a colostomy bag Led by the Universities of Leeds and Birmingham, the international trial treated patients with early-stage rectal cancer, with combinations of chemotherapy
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A major trial has found that patients with rectal cancer may be able to avoid major surgery and the need for a colostomy bag Led by the Universities of Leeds and Birmingham, the international trial treated patients with early-stage rectal cancer, with combinations of chemotherapy and radiotherapy instead of surgery The findings, published in Lancet Oncology and funded by Cancer Research UK, said the initial results suggested that organ‑preserving treatment may be a realistic option for many people with early rectal cancer Cancer Research UK said the findings could be "life-changing for thousands of people" Up to 14,000 people are diagnosed with rectal cancer in the UK every year and of these, around one in three are at an early stage, according to the University of Leeds Patients are usually treated with a complex surgical procedure called a Total Mesorectal Excision (TME), which involves the complete removal of the rectum, the surrounding fat, and lymph nodes

The scheme is simil Weir Mill, which sits under the arches of Stockport’s iconic railway viaduct, has been driven forward by Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC), a partnership between Stockport council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Pervert secretly recorded people in gym changing rooms including child Daniel Michalowski claimed he filmed 'out of curiosity' News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:53, 24 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Daniel Michalowski leaving Manchester Crown Court (Im A pervert secretly recorded a number of people as they got dressed in changing rooms at a gym in Wythenshawe . Daniel Michalowski stuck his phone under a cubicle and filmed up to 12 women, one man and a child over a three-month period He was caught out after an employee at the gym spotted Michalowski's phone filming him under his cubicle. Manchester Crown Court heard that the 45-year-old also made a number of online searches for voyeurism on pornography sites Having previously pleaded guilty to offences of voyeurism and taking an indecent photo of a child, Michalowski, of Wythenshawe, was handed a suspended jail term on Monday (August 24) Prosecuting, Lawrence Rainford said that earlier this year, as the male staff member finished his shift at 9pm, he met his partner before they went to get changed in the unisex changing rooms "He noticed the presence of a phone from the adjoining cubicle being withdrawn," he said. "He took the decision to knock on the door and confront the individual."

title: The Mancunian Way: Ear today, corn tomorrow

evidence_packet.title: The Mancunian Way: Ear today, corn tomorrow
evidence_packet.lead: “But some people are coming and shouting at us.
evidence_packet.summary: “But some people are coming and shouting at us. We’re not British but we came here legally, we studied here and got work visas, but we couldn’t find jobs, so we started this small stall business, and Market Street is the best street.” Danny, 29, is president of the Market Street
evidence_packet.evidence_text: “But some people are coming and shouting at us. We’re not British but we came here legally, we studied here and got work visas, but we couldn’t find jobs, so we started this small stall business, and Market Street is the best street.” Danny, 29, is president of the Market Street traders WhatsApp group. He came to the UK from Pakistan to study for his master's degree and sells sweetcorn and chocolate strawberries from carts on the busy city centre street But recently, he’s had a problem. Someone using glasses with a small camera inside recorded him and put the video on TikTok Licenced seller Danny wasn’t aware his stall was being filmed during the encounter and said he felt upset at how the video was captured. It’s part of a growing trend of footage being shared online about spots in Manchester such as Market Street and Piccadilly Gardens View 5 Images Danny, 29, who runs a sweetcorn business on Market Street. Image by LDR Declan Carey. (Image: Declan Carey / Local Democracy Reporting Service) And as Declan reports, this sly tactic is becoming increasingly common as tensions grow about the future of Market Street. When he visited on a grey Thursday afternoon, he found at least four different stalls selling sweetcorn in various flavours

No timeline has been given on when the building will reopen From today (August 24), Royton Library will temporarily close while works are carried out to repair flooring within the building and further investigations to take place. Oldham Council said they would give a reopening date as soon as more information becomes available Subnum Hariff-Khan, Head of Heritage, Libraries and Arts for Oldham Council, said: “We understand that Royton Library is a valued community resource and a place that many residents rely on, so we appreciate that this temporary closure may cause some inconvenience. We’re exploring “These works are essential to ensure the building remains safe, welcoming and fit for the future. Throughout the closure, customers will still be able to access library services at our other libraries across the borough, as well as a wide range of digital resources online “We would like to thank residents for their patience and understanding while this work takes place

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Queues and 'chaotic' scenes as people get ready to leave Manchester for Stockport The historic site was transformed with the help of £60m with one man described being left 'emotional' as the once 'orange' River Mersey is now 'lovely and gree People have been left ’emotional’ with dozens ‘queueing around the block’ to try and get a home inside Stockport ’s ‘really cool’ Weir Mill development. The historic site was transformed with the help of £60m The former cotton mill on the banks of the River Mersey, which dates back to 1790, has been transformed into a trendy neighbourhood featuring apartments, bars, restaurants, coffee spots and shops . It’s a project people have been eagerly awaiting, with many trying to sneak a peek Across the site’s new and refurbished buildings , there are 253 apartments for rent which will sit alongside a number of businesses including a riverside Italian restaurant, a wine bar that will be a ‘UK first’, a bookshop, and a bar focused on women’s sports. The scheme is simil Weir Mill, which sits under the arches of Stockport’s iconic railway viaduct, has been driven forward by Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC), a partnership between Stockport council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Pervert secretly recorded people in gym changing rooms including child Daniel Michalowski claimed he filmed 'out of curiosity' News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:53, 24 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Daniel Michalowski leaving Manchester Crown Court (Im A pervert secretly recorded a number of people as they got dressed in changing rooms at a gym in Wythenshawe . Daniel Michalowski stuck his phone under a cubicle and filmed up to 12 women, one man and a child over a three-month period He was caught out after an employee at the gym spotted Michalowski's phone filming him under his cubicle. Manchester Crown Court heard that the 45-year-old also made a number of online searches for voyeurism on pornography sites Having previously pleaded guilty to offences of voyeurism and taking an indecent photo of a child, Michalowski, of Wythenshawe, was handed a suspended jail term on Monday (August 24) Prosecuting, Lawrence Rainford said that earlier this year, as the male staff member finished his shift at 9pm, he met his partner before they went to get changed in the unisex changing rooms "He noticed the presence of a phone from the adjoining cubicle being withdrawn," he said. "He took the decision to knock on the door and confront the individual."

evidence_packet.lead: “But some people are coming and shouting at us.
evidence_packet.summary: “But some people are coming and shouting at us. We’re not British but we came here legally, we studied here and got work visas, but we couldn’t find jobs, so we started this small stall business, and Market Street is the best street.” Danny, 29, is president of the Market Street
evidence_packet.evidence_text: “But some people are coming and shouting at us. We’re not British but we came here legally, we studied here and got work visas, but we couldn’t find jobs, so we started this small stall business, and Market Street is the best street.” Danny, 29, is president of the Market Street traders WhatsApp group. He came to the UK from Pakistan to study for his master's degree and sells sweetcorn and chocolate strawberries from carts on the busy city centre street But recently, he’s had a problem. Someone using glasses with a small camera inside recorded him and put the video on TikTok Licenced seller Danny wasn’t aware his stall was being filmed during the encounter and said he felt upset at how the video was captured. It’s part of a growing trend of footage being shared online about spots in Manchester such as Market Street and Piccadilly Gardens View 5 Images Danny, 29, who runs a sweetcorn business on Market Street. Image by LDR Declan Carey. (Image: Declan Carey / Local Democracy Reporting Service) And as Declan reports, this sly tactic is becoming increasingly common as tensions grow about the future of Market Street. When he visited on a grey Thursday afternoon, he found at least four different stalls selling sweetcorn in various flavours

title: Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs

evidence_packet.title: Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs
evidence_packet.lead: Wythenshawe Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs A large policing operation was in place in south Manchester over the weekend News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:56, 24 Aug 2026 View Ima Police made just five arrest
evidence_packet.summary: Wythenshawe Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs A large policing operation was in place in south Manchester over the weekend News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:56, 24 Aug 2026 View Ima Police made just five arrest
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wythenshawe Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs A large policing operation was in place in south Manchester over the weekend News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:56, 24 Aug 2026 View Ima Police made just five arrests as 70,000 music fans attended huge gigs in Wythenshawe over the weekend The Cure and Lewis Capaldi played sold-out headline gigs at Wythenshawe Park on Friday (August 21) and Saturday (August 22). A large policing operation was in place as thousands descended on the outdoor venue In an update issued today (Monday), Greater Manchester Police said five arrests were made across the two days. The arrests were 'mainly for alcohol offences', a force spokesperson said Officers used Live Facial Recognition (LFR) technology as part of the policing operation, but no arrests were made as a result. Chief Superintendent Danny O'Neil said: "There was some traffic disruption around the event "We would like to thank attendees, residents and motorists for their patience and encourage people to plan their journeys in advance when travelling in the area to avoid disruption

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Royton Oldham library forced to temporarily close two years after £4m reburbishment No timeline has been given on when the building will reopen. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 13:42, 24 Aug 2026 Updated 14:09, 24 Aug 2026 View Im An Oldham library has closed less than two years after £4m was spent refurbishing it. No timeline has been given on when the building will reopen From today (August 24), Royton Library will temporarily close while works are carried out to repair flooring within the building and further investigations to take place. Oldham Council said they would give a reopening date as soon as more information becomes available Subnum Hariff-Khan, Head of Heritage, Libraries and Arts for Oldham Council, said: “We understand that Royton Library is a valued community resource and a place that many residents rely on, so we appreciate that this temporary closure may cause some inconvenience. We’re exploring “These works are essential to ensure the building remains safe, welcoming and fit for the future. Throughout the closure, customers will still be able to access library services at our other libraries across the borough, as well as a wide range of digital resources online “We would like to thank residents for their patience and understanding while this work takes place

evidence_packet.summary: Courts Flower arranging class descends into chaos as Wigan pupil launches protein drink at tutor who slated coursework 'Childish' Lorraine Jae, 51, punched Tracey Musker and threw a protein drink at her victim, hitting her on the chin News Lee Grimsdi A woman has been ordered to
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Flower arranging class descends into chaos as Wigan pupil launches protein drink at tutor who slated coursework 'Childish' Lorraine Jae, 51, punched Tracey Musker and threw a protein drink at her victim, hitting her on the chin News Lee Grimsdi A woman has been ordered to pay compensation after a flower arranging class ended in a foul-mouthed tirades and violence. Lorraine Jae, from Leigh , punched fellow student Tracey Musker and threw a drink at her The 51-year-old, a court was told, had a meltdown in a college classroom and grabbed her coat due to criticism of her coursework by their tutor. As other students attending the floristry lesson at St Helens College, in Merseyside, looked on, Jae told Miss Musker to 'shut the f*** Then when Miss Musker laughed off the abuse, Liverpool Magistrates' Court heard how Jae ran at her, punched her in the face before picking up a full protein drink carton and throwing it at her. The fortified beverage hit Miss Musker on the chin The fight was broken up by other students before Jae stormed out of the classroom Miss Musker, who received first aid at the scene, suffered bruises and a cut to her chin and a mark on her lip. She did not require hospital treatment

title: Andy Burnham to hand Greater Manchester £529m to build thousands of affordable homes

evidence_packet.title: Andy Burnham to hand Greater Manchester £529m to build thousands of affordable homes
evidence_packet.lead: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham to hand Greater Manchester £529m to build thousands of affordable homes The money is part of £10bn being handed out to regional mayors, councils, and housing associations across the country View 2 Images Tens of thousands of News Hannah Richardson 22:30
evidence_packet.summary: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham to hand Greater Manchester £529m to build thousands of affordable homes The money is part of £10bn being handed out to regional mayors, councils, and housing associations across the country View 2 Images Tens of thousands of News Hannah Richardson 22:30
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham to hand Greater Manchester £529m to build thousands of affordable homes The money is part of £10bn being handed out to regional mayors, councils, and housing associations across the country View 2 Images Tens of thousands of News Hannah Richardson 22:30, 24 Aug 2026 Updated 22:59, 24 Aug 2026 Andy Burnham is handing out £10 billion in a bid to ‘build the country out of a housing crisis’ as he says ‘no child should be raised in a hostel room’ Nationally, almost 180,000 children are growing up without a permanent home, the Government added. The allocations, which are wave one of Labour ’s £39bn 10-year Social and Affordable Homes Programme, aim to help families ‘trapped in temporary accommodation or stuck on housing wa The Prime Minister said the cash will go to regional mayors, councils, housing associations and other providers to be spent on building ‘genuinely affordable homes’. Around 60pc of the more than 70,000 properties to be funded through the allocations are expected to be social rent Of the money up for grabs, Greater Manchester will be allocated £529 million – the largest share of any of the six mayoral areas that will benefit from this round. This is expected to deliver around 4,400 new homes, the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government said In November 2025, it was announced that Greater Manchester would ultimately benefit from £1.8bn from the Social and Affordable Homes Programme

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Queues and 'chaotic' scenes as people get ready to leave Manchester for Stockport The historic site was transformed with the help of £60m with one man described being left 'emotional' as the once 'orange' River Mersey is now 'lovely and gree People have been left ’emotional’ with dozens ‘queueing around the block’ to try and get a home inside Stockport ’s ‘really cool’ Weir Mill development. The historic site was transformed with the help of £60m The former cotton mill on the banks of the River Mersey, which dates back to 1790, has been transformed into a trendy neighbourhood featuring apartments, bars, restaurants, coffee spots and shops . It’s a project people have been eagerly awaiting, with many trying to sneak a peek Across the site’s new and refurbished buildings , there are 253 apartments for rent which will sit alongside a number of businesses including a riverside Italian restaurant, a wine bar that will be a ‘UK first’, a bookshop, and a bar focused on women’s sports. The scheme is simil Weir Mill, which sits under the arches of Stockport’s iconic railway viaduct, has been driven forward by Stockport Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC), a partnership between Stockport council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Pervert secretly recorded people in gym changing rooms including child Daniel Michalowski claimed he filmed 'out of curiosity' News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:53, 24 Aug 2026 View 3 Images Daniel Michalowski leaving Manchester Crown Court (Im A pervert secretly recorded a number of people as they got dressed in changing rooms at a gym in Wythenshawe . Daniel Michalowski stuck his phone under a cubicle and filmed up to 12 women, one man and a child over a three-month period He was caught out after an employee at the gym spotted Michalowski's phone filming him under his cubicle. Manchester Crown Court heard that the 45-year-old also made a number of online searches for voyeurism on pornography sites Having previously pleaded guilty to offences of voyeurism and taking an indecent photo of a child, Michalowski, of Wythenshawe, was handed a suspended jail term on Monday (August 24) Prosecuting, Lawrence Rainford said that earlier this year, as the male staff member finished his shift at 9pm, he met his partner before they went to get changed in the unisex changing rooms "He noticed the presence of a phone from the adjoining cubicle being withdrawn," he said. "He took the decision to knock on the door and confront the individual."

evidence_packet.summary: “But some people are coming and shouting at us. We’re not British but we came here legally, we studied here and got work visas, but we couldn’t find jobs, so we started this small stall business, and Market Street is the best street.” Danny, 29, is president of the Market Street
evidence_packet.evidence_text: “But some people are coming and shouting at us. We’re not British but we came here legally, we studied here and got work visas, but we couldn’t find jobs, so we started this small stall business, and Market Street is the best street.” Danny, 29, is president of the Market Street traders WhatsApp group. He came to the UK from Pakistan to study for his master's degree and sells sweetcorn and chocolate strawberries from carts on the busy city centre street But recently, he’s had a problem. Someone using glasses with a small camera inside recorded him and put the video on TikTok Licenced seller Danny wasn’t aware his stall was being filmed during the encounter and said he felt upset at how the video was captured. It’s part of a growing trend of footage being shared online about spots in Manchester such as Market Street and Piccadilly Gardens View 5 Images Danny, 29, who runs a sweetcorn business on Market Street. Image by LDR Declan Carey. (Image: Declan Carey / Local Democracy Reporting Service) And as Declan reports, this sly tactic is becoming increasingly common as tensions grow about the future of Market Street. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Police in haz-mat suits swarm Stockport street after 'liquid drugs lab' arrests Two arrests were made at Salford Quays in Salford Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 16:55, 24 Aug 2026 Updated 17:57, 24 Aug 2026 View 4 Images Police at the s Police and firefighters wearing hazardous materials suits are carrying out searches of a commercial unit on a street in Stockport over the suspected production of 'liquid drugs' Two men aged in their 20s have been arrested in Salford Quays, Salford, in connection with the discovery of the suspected drugs lab in Stockport, Greater Manchester Police said Both men were held on suspicion of the exportation of Class A and B drugs, and they both remained in custody for questioning on Monday afternoon. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Royton Oldham library forced to temporarily close two years after £4m reburbishment No timeline has been given on when the building will reopen. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 13:42, 24 Aug 2026 Updated 14:09, 24 Aug 2026 View Im An Oldham library has closed less than two years after £4m was spent refurbishing it. No timeline has been given on when the building will reopen From today (August 24), Royton Library will temporarily close while works are carried out to repair flooring within the building and further investigations to take place. Oldham Council said they would give a reopening date as soon as more information becomes available Subnum Hariff-Khan, Head of Heritage, Libraries and Arts for Oldham Council, said: “We understand that Royton Library is a valued community resource and a place that many residents rely on, so we appreciate that this temporary closure may cause some inconvenience. We’re exploring “These works are essential to ensure the building remains safe, welcoming and fit for the future. Throughout the closure, customers will still be able to access library services at our other libraries across the borough, as well as a wide range of digital resources online “We would like to thank residents for their patience and understanding while this work takes place

title: Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs

evidence_packet.title: Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs
evidence_packet.lead: Wythenshawe Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs A large policing operation was in place in south Manchester over the weekend News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:56, 24 Aug 2026 View Ima Police made just five arrest
evidence_packet.summary: Wythenshawe Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs A large policing operation was in place in south Manchester over the weekend News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:56, 24 Aug 2026 View Ima Police made just five arrest
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wythenshawe Wythenshawe Park arrests made as 70,000 attend huge Lewis Capaldi and The Cure gigs A large policing operation was in place in south Manchester over the weekend News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:56, 24 Aug 2026 View Ima Police made just five arrests as 70,000 music fans attended huge gigs in Wythenshawe over the weekend The Cure and Lewis Capaldi played sold-out headline gigs at Wythenshawe Park on Friday (August 21) and Saturday (August 22). A large policing operation was in place as thousands descended on the outdoor venue In an update issued today (Monday), Greater Manchester Police said five arrests were made across the two days. The arrests were 'mainly for alcohol offences', a force spokesperson said Officers used Live Facial Recognition (LFR) technology as part of the policing operation, but no arrests were made as a result. Chief Superintendent Danny O'Neil said: "There was some traffic disruption around the event "We would like to thank attendees, residents and motorists for their patience and encourage people to plan their journeys in advance when travelling in the area to avoid disruption

evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

evidence_packet.title: Manchester Race Across the World star Jo Gardiner dies year after son
evidence_packet.lead: Jo Gardiner, 61, died "following a long and courageous battle with cancer", her family said Gardiner, a physiotherapist from Manchester, travelled across South America with her son Sam in the second series of the BBC show, which aired in 2020 Her family said she was "one of a kin
evidence_packet.summary: Jo Gardiner, 61, died "following a long and courageous battle with cancer", her family said Gardiner, a physiotherapist from Manchester, travelled across South America with her son Sam in the second series of the BBC show, which aired in 2020 Her family said she was "one of a kin
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Jo Gardiner, 61, died "following a long and courageous battle with cancer", her family said Gardiner, a physiotherapist from Manchester, travelled across South America with her son Sam in the second series of the BBC show, which aired in 2020 Her family said she was "one of a kind" who "lived fully, fiercely and never did anything by halves" Her son, Sam, who she appeared with on the show, died in June 2025 after his car came off the road and crashed The mother and son competed on Race Across The World because Gardiner wanted to experience a travel adventure with Sam, who had ADHD They competed against four other pairs of contestants racing from Mexico City down to Ushuaia in Argentina

title: Mum to travel to US over Lucy Harrison shooting investigation

evidence_packet.title: Mum to travel to US over Lucy Harrison shooting investigation
evidence_packet.lead: Lucy Harrison, 23, from Warrington, was shot in the chest on 10 January 2025 in Prosper, near Dallas Police in the town investigated her death as possible manslaughter but no criminal case was brought against her father Kris Harrison after a grand jury in Collin County declined t
evidence_packet.summary: Lucy Harrison, 23, from Warrington, was shot in the chest on 10 January 2025 in Prosper, near Dallas Police in the town investigated her death as possible manslaughter but no criminal case was brought against her father Kris Harrison after a grand jury in Collin County declined t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Lucy Harrison, 23, from Warrington, was shot in the chest on 10 January 2025 in Prosper, near Dallas Police in the town investigated her death as possible manslaughter but no criminal case was brought against her father Kris Harrison after a grand jury in Collin County declined to indict him Lucy Harrison's mother Jane Coates said she hopes to meet the district attorney and call for a fresh investigation. The Collin County District Attorney's Office has been approached for comment Harrison, a 23-year-old fashion buyer, was shot by her father at his home in Texas the day before she was due to fly home to the UK A grand jury in Collin County later decided there was insufficient evidence to bring criminal charges after Kris Harrison said the Glock handgun discharged accidentally while he was showing it to his daughter In February this year, a coroner in England concluded Harrison had been unlawfully killed, finding that her father's actions amounted to gross negligence manslaughter under UK law

title: Council secures court order following unauthorised encampment at Oldham Edge

evidence_packet.title: Council secures court order following unauthorised encampment at Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Council has secured a court order requiring the removal of an unauthorised encampment from Oldham Edge. Council officers first visited the site on Thursday 6th August following concerns from residents and people using the park. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August. As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their vehicles and belongings. The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime. After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment. A Council spokesperson said: “We understand the concerns raised by residents and people using Oldham Edge, and we thank them for their patience while we followed the legal process. “We always try to resolve unauthorised encampments through discussion and voluntary cooperation wherever possible. However, when the site was not vacated as agreed, it became necessary to take further action. “We worked closely with Greater Manchester Police throughout to make sure the situation was handled lawfully and proportionately. “The encampment has now left and our cleansing team has completed the clean-up, allowing the area to be returned to the local community.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Shopping, sport, art, dra Live theatre, the best of cinema and one of the country's finest museums: The Quays offers a fantastic choice of things to do and see. Imperial War Museum North and The Lowry are vibrant and exciting examples of contemporary architecture, the contents as stunning as the setting a Whether you're a shopaholic or just someone who likes a bargain, the opening of the Quayside MediaCityUK has made The Quays a mecca for the discerning shopper with big-name brand shops and stores offering discount prices - up to 70 per cent lower than the high street - all year r There's no better place to find top sport action than The Quays. Home to two of the most renowned clubs in British sport - Manchester United and Lancashire County Cricket Club , The Quays is the area to head for when wanting the best in football and cricket. Both have official sh Built in 2000 at the booming Salford Quays, this astonishing building is a shrine to all things art, with galleries, theatres, workshops, cafes and shops. It's worth a visit just to sit outside and admire the vision in metal and glass. But you'd be missing out on a whole world of Watersports The Salford Watersports Centre at The Quays is a unique sporting venue which is well placed and perfect for taking to the water. Whether it's for fun or serious competition, the Salford Watersports Centre is the place to head for

evidence_packet.evidence_text: For two decades Sounds From The Other City has been championing new music, local promoters and the off-kilter beauty of Salford, the oft-overlooked ‘other city’ to Manchester The unique model of SFTOC means that the festival curation is ever-evolving; each year the festival invites a selection of the region’s best promoters and selectors, give them a stage and ask them to book the artists that most excite them The festival has hosted early-day performances from artists as diverse as Black Country, New Road, The Ting Tings, Alabaster de Plume, Alt-J, The Ting Tings, BiPolar Sunshine, Hannah Peel, GoGo Penguin right through to 2017’s Mercury Music Prize winner Sampha, BBC Sound of 2018 n Join in for another round of Sounds From The Other City, celebrating the very best in new music, performance and art General release tickets are on sale now and going fast. Get yours below and join the party of the year on this May Day Bank Holiday Sunday Chapel Street and the Crescent neighbourhood - see SFTOC website for all venues taking part

It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
